clue.text: Burn to get ahead fast

explanation.surface: Advice to a driver: put your foot down and burn rubber to get in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is both to singe with heat and, colloquially, to drive or ride at breakneck speed.

clue.text: Eric's association with club is sadly in the melting-pot

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of the two words before are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Eric's link with a club has, alas, been thrown into turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for melting metals at high heat is a melting-pot.

clue.text: Congress receives one Trade Union with formal ceremony

indicators.note: receives means the congress word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or congress
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A congress welcomes a union delegate with pomp and ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by prescribed rite means doing something ceremonially.

clue.text: Encouraged to learn incomplete tender's out of order

parts.note: to hear of something is to learn it

indicators.note: out of order means the shortened letters are jumbled
incomplete means the word tender loses its final letter

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered to hear that part of a bid was not in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops R from TENDER to leave TENDE; 'out of order' shuffles that to TENED after HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given heart or confidence is to be encouraged.

clue.text: Many make a home with lair or set

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so 'many'
to make a home somewhere is to live there
an animal's lair is its den

explanation.surface: A badger settles into its den, or set, along with many others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like another word for a badger's den beside 'lair', but it defines: the Cliveden Set was the 1930s circle of political figures who met at Cliveden, the Astors' country house in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The house's name stands for the influential interwar social circle known after it, so the place name is used for that group.

clue.text: French version of card-trick?

parts.note: the three-card trick asks the mark to 'find the lady', and the French saying means exactly that

explanation.surface: What would the conjuror's game be called in France?
explanation.walkthrough: In the three-card trick (three-card monte) the victim must find the queen; the French phrase means 'look for the woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French proverb literally translates as 'find the lady', the patter of the card swindle.

clue.text: Severe oil trouble in outlet

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the outlet word

parts.note: a vent is an outlet for air or gas

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of oil are disturbed

explanation.surface: A serious problem with oil in a pipe outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns OIL into IOL, which 'in' places inside VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme force or intensity, as in a fierce storm, makes something severe.

clue.text: Decide at Assembly to make act of devotion

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together, so the letters of decide at are reassembled

explanation.surface: A council resolves to perform a pious act.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote or consecrate something to a cause or deity is a formal act of offering.

clue.text: Veto photographic evidence

explanation.surface: A ban is put on the photographs used as proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or 'no' vote, and also the reversed film image from which prints are made.

clue.text: One of the containers may meet the situation

explanation.surface: A packing tip: one of these bags may be just right for the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling case is a container for luggage, and read as two words it says 'suit the case', i.e. fit the circumstances.

clue.text: Snack for a stolen pet

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a dog is a common pet

explanation.surface: A thief walks off with someone's pet to get a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage in a bun is a familiar street-food snack.

clue.text: Soldier acting in disguise in vast production

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: acting in disguise means the letters of the word acting appear in a changed form

explanation.surface: A soldier plays a part in costume in an enormous stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges ACTING to GANTIC after GI; 'production' is surface padding beside the definition 'vast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous or huge in size is vast.

clue.text: Teach quiet arrangement to jazz fan

indicators.note: an arrangement here is a reordering of the letters given before it

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Teach a quiet musical arrangement to a lover of jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip follower of swing music in 1940s slang is a jazz fan.

clue.text: Sir, your weapon-destiny!

parts.note: a lance is a knight's weapon
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Addressing a knight: sir, your weapon will decide your fate!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir' defines by example: this is Sir Lancelot of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The most famous knight of the Round Table is addressed by that title, so the title stands for the knight.

clue.text: How a winger beats the opposite insides?

definitions.text: How a winger beats the opposite insides?

parts.words: How a winger beats the opposite insides?
parts.note: a wide player goes round the outside of the opposing inside forwards or defenders

explanation.surface: How does a wing forward get past the opposing inside players?
explanation.walkthrough: Wing and inside are football and rugby positions: the winger gets round the sides of the inside men.
explanation.definitionFit: To get round the side of an opponent's line is the military and sporting term for passing them on the wing.

clue.text: Paper by Oxford scholar

explanation.surface: A note written on fine paper by a learned Oxford man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional size of printing paper, and also the name for a foundation scholar at Magdalen College, Oxford.

clue.text: A rare medical find back here in Guyana

indicators.note: back means the found letters are read in reverse order
a find is something discovered within, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: An uncommon medical discovery made in Guyana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' takes ARAREMED from 'A rare med(ical)'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of Guyana around its river gives its name to brown cane sugar, so the place is in that country.

clue.text: She's entitled to go to dining-room in college

definitions.text: She's entitled to go to dining-room in college

parts.words: She's entitled to go to dining-room in college
parts.note: entitled 'Lady', with a dining-room 'Hall' after her, she names an Oxford college

explanation.surface: A titled woman has the right to dine in college hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Margaret Hall is an Oxford college: the title Lady before her, the Hall (dining-room) after.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman's first name sits between a title and a word for a dining-room in an Oxford college name.

clue.text: The winding Eden Vale

indicators.note: a winding course twists, so the letters of Eden are turned about

explanation.surface: A river called the Eden meanders through a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden is a real English river, which helps the picture of a winding stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow wooded valley in dialect is a vale.

clue.text: Line up on time for cavalry training

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to dress ranks is to line them up in military drill
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Soldiers line up punctually for horse drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Training a horse in precise movements is the classical riding discipline taught to cavalry.

clue.text: Originally the name of the game was to make a bit of money

definitions.text: Originally the name of the game was to make a bit of money

parts.words: Originally the name of the game was to make a bit of money
parts.note: the word names a card game and also an old French gold coin, a bit of money

explanation.surface: At first the whole point was simply to earn some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the name of the game' is the idiom for the main aim, but literally it is a card game's name, which is also that of a French gold coin bearing the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game and the French twenty-franc gold coin share the emperor's name.

clue.text: Will he put you on later, say, summa cum laude?

definitions.text: Will he put you on later, say, summa cum laude?

parts.words: Will he put you on later, say, summa cum laude?
parts.note: summa cum laude means 'with highest praise', and someone who lays it on thick praises you to the skies

explanation.surface: Will the examiner later award you the top honours grade?
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin graduation phrase points to university results, but read literally it means praising in the highest terms, which is what a flatterer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatterer showers excessive praise, the kind given with the highest honours.

clue.text: Entertaining my claim as employer

parts.note: an employer makes use of staff, so might say of them 'I'm using', which run together suggests the word for entertaining

explanation.surface: My boast as a boss is that I'm fun to work for.
explanation.walkthrough: An employer uses people, so says 'I'm using'; said quickly, that phrase is the adjective for entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny or diverting is a synonym for entertaining.

clue.text: Urge prize for example of tableware

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
a cup is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: Push for a prize that is a piece of china.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for a boiled egg is a piece of breakfast crockery.

clue.text: Perfect way to work for a period

parts.note: full means complete or perfect
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: The ideal route to a job takes a certain time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' is the American name for the punctuation mark ending a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot ending a sentence is called a period in American usage.

clue.text: Can the intrepid say they're so regretful?

definitions.text: Can the intrepid say they're so regretful?

parts.words: Can the intrepid say they're so regretful?
parts.note: the fearless cannot claim to be scared, yet the polite apology 'I'm ... ' uses that same word for being sorry

explanation.surface: Can brave people ever express regret?
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both frightened, which the intrepid are not, and sorry, as in a polite apology.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry to say something is expressed with the same word as fearful.

clue.text: Authorities given by electors and held by officers

indicators.note: held by means the word and sits inside the officers word

parts.note: mates are officers on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: Powers granted by voters are seized by military officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters confer on winners official authority to act, called the electoral commission or authorisation.

clue.text: Negation of reform is a tragedy

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of Negation are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rejecting reform is a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the play by Sophocles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' play about Oedipus's daughter is a classical Greek drama of the tragic kind.

clue.text: Alias Yorick, the sentimental journeyman

explanation.surface: A man going by the name Yorick sets off on an emotional trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote as Parson Yorick and was author of A Sentimental Journey, so he is that traveller.
